c.tagline: A storybook Alsatian town of half-timbered houses, flower-lined canals, and Christmas-market fame
langs: Alsatian (regional dialect, still spoken by some)

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small market stalls

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The compact old town is entirely walkable and one of the best-preserved in France; a car is useful for the surrounding Alsace Wine Route villages

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with visitors of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded market season is the main concern

hood_landmark.La Petite Venise (Little Venice): La Petite Venise's canal-side half-timbered houses
hood_landmark.Old Town Center: Saint Martin's Church and the Ancienne Douane
hood_landmark.Unterlinden Quarter: The Unterlinden Museum and Isenheim Altarpiece
hood_landmark.Krutenau: The Krutenau district's former fishmonger and tanner streets
hood_landmark.Christmas Market Squares: Place Jeanne d'Arc and Place des Dominicains market squares

avoid.reason: Christmas-market crowds attract occasional pickpockets in the old town; otherwise usual awareness.

hood_desc: The postcard canal district of flower-draped half-timbered houses, best explored by a short boat ride or a stroll along the Lauch river.
The pedestrianized medieval core with the largest church and most shops and restaurants; the natural base for any visit.
Home to Colmar's top museum, housed in a former convent, with an easy walk to the surrounding old streets.
A historic working-class quarter of the old town, quieter than the main tourist core but just as picturesque.
The squares that host Colmar's famous Christmas markets each winter, ringed by mulled-wine stalls and crafts.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.sys: Trace Colmar Agglomération urban bus network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: The old town is pedestrian-friendly; a car is useful for the Alsace Wine Route villages

transport.air: Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg EuroAirport (BSL/MLH), about 45 min away; Strasbourg Airport is a further alternative
transport.train: Direct TGV/TER rail connections to Strasbourg (35 min) and Paris (under 3 hr)
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to Alsace Wine Route villages
transport.car: Well connected via the A35 motorway; the old town is best explored on foot

airport.name: Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg EuroAirport
airport.transport: Train via Mulhouse, shuttle bus, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
